overview.description: Zecchinetta (Lansquenet) is an Italian banking/gambling game. Banker vs players. 40-card Italian deck. Banker deals 2 player cards + 1 banker card face-up. Players bet on player cards. Banker draws cards: match player card = banker pays; match banker card = banker wins all bets. New unmatched cards become additional betting options.

history.origins: Zecchinetta is the Italian variant of Lansquenet, one of Europe's oldest recorded banking games. Lansquenet is named after the German Landsknecht (medieval mercenary) and appears in Rabelais' Gargantua (1542). The Italian form became especially associated with Sicily and southern Italy and was carried to the USA by Italian immigrants as Ziginette. Traditionally played with a 40-card Italian pack, it remains popular in private play in Italy despite being illegal in public places.
timeline: 19th century: French Lansquenet documented; Italian Zecchinetta variant popular in Sicily.
history.evolution: One of Europe's oldest banking games.

rules.objective: Players: bet card matches drawn before banker's. Banker: collect when banker card matches.
rules.gameplay: Deal 2 player cards + 1 banker card. Players bet on player cards. Draw cards: match player = banker pays. Match banker = banker wins all. New rank = new betting card. Bank passes after banker match.
keyRules: Banker card match = banker wins all
New ranks create new betting cards

phases.label: Deal initial cards
phases.notes: Banker reveals top two cards for players (Per voi), then third for banker (Per me).

phases.label: Place bets
phases.notes: Players bet on the two player cards within banker min and max.

phases.label: Banker reveals cards
phases.notes: Banker turns up cards one at a time; match player card banker wins that card's bets, match banker card banker pays and bank passes right.

phases.label: Settle
phases.notes: Resolve payouts; bank passes to right if banker lost.

edgeCases.text: If first two cards (Per voi) are equal rank, reshuffle and redeal with same banker.
If third card (Per me) matches a player card, banker wins all bets and bank passes to the right.
New rank (carta buona) becomes an extra betting card; players may bet on it.
Rank already seen twice (carta mala) is discarded and deal continues.

engine.deckDescription: Italian 40-card pack used for Zecchinetta: no 8s, 9s or 10s. Four suits (Coins, Swords, Cups, Batons or regional equivalents). Ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, Fante (Jack), Cavallo (Knight), Re (King).
engine.suitDescription: Italian suits: Coins (Denari), Swords (Spade), Cups (Coppe), Batons (Bastoni). Latin-suited designs are sometimes used in Italy for this game.
engine.rankDescription: Stripped 40-card ranks: Ace, 2 through 7, Fante (Jack), Cavallo (Knight), Re (King). Only rank identity matters for matching; suits are irrelevant.
engine.dealPattern: Two cards face-up for players (Per voi), one face-up for banker (Per me); no cards to hand.

notApplicableReasons.shedding: Zecchinetta is a banking and matching game, not a shedding game.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: Zecchinetta uses banker-reveal and bet resolution, not a play-to-capture fishing mechanic.
